text:
jamie: Quick thread — proposal for a defensive capacity-smoothing layer on the Dedicated GPU pool orchestration. Goal: reduce flip-flopping when lots of small tenants request short bursts.

sasha: +1 this has bitten us. high-level: smoothing at allocator level or admission level?

jamie: thinking allocator-level intent smoothing. keep raw intent timeseries but apply a hysteresis window and a capped rolling average to convert into \"admissible intent\". that way the operator sees stable decisions instead of thrash.

liam: can you sketch the math? curious about tail latency impact when we delay admitting a real spike.

jamie: sure — rough: admissible_intent(t) = max(admissible_intent(t-1) * (1 - decay), rolling_avg(intent, W)) clipped by tenant_max. decay ~ 0.15, W ~ 30s for bursty workloads. tradeoff: small added admission delay vs noise immunity.

mira: what about burst credits? we already have tenant burst buckets that let short spikes through. smoothing shouldn't block credits, only influence autoscale decisions.

jamie: exactly — credits are orthogonal. admission path: if tenant has burst_credits > 0 -> bypass smoothing. else smoothing influences reservation requests to orchestration.

sasha: edge case: two tenants alternate bursts and collectively saturate pool; smoothing might hide oscillation and delay scaling up. how do we ensure safety?

jamie: add a transfer function for aggregate headroom: if aggregate_admissible > threshold for M consecutive windows -> escalate to provisional scale request that bypasses per-tenant hysteresis. threshold tuned by pool size.

liam: can we implement this as a thin shim in the operator so we don't refactor allocator right away? like a sidecar that consumes intents, publishes smoothed intents to operator API?

jamie: yep, prototyping as a standalone \"intent-filter\" service is preferred. operator API already accepts intent blobs. intent-filter would: subscribe -> smooth -> annotate metadata (bypass flags, confidence) -> push back. minimal surface change.

mira: telemetry needs: raw vs smoothed intent timeseries + reasons for bypass. add tags so console can show when smoothing prevented a scale event.

jamie: agreed. sample metrics: intent_raw_qps, intent_smoothed_qps, smoothed_bypass_count, provisional_escalations. dashboards + alert: provisional_escalations > 3/min -> ops review.

sasha: implementation checklist?

jamie: early plan: 1) intent-filter service proto (1 week), 2) operator accept annotated intents (small API bump) (2 days), 3) unit tests + sim harness with synthetic tenants (1 week), 4) canary on staging pool (3 days).

liam: can we add a toggle flag per-cluster to disable smoothing? customer-facing dedicated tenants might want raw behavior.

jamie: yes - per-pool feature flag + per-tenant opt-out. default ON for system pools, OFF for isolated enterprise pools.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created canary job pipeline \"intent-filter/canary\" -> queued. :rocket:

mira: one more thought — ensure that rollback path is fast: if provisional_escalation triggers and then rolls back, we should amortize cost by adding a short cool-down preventing immediate downscale.

jamie: noted. add cooldown param to operator: downscale_cooldown = max(60s, 2 * smoothing_window).

sasha: Solid. i'm happy for jamie to spin an RFC doc with diagrams and the sim results.I'll review. :thumbsup:

jamie: will write up RFC and attach synthetic workload traces. thanks all.
